trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access to electronic personal information) of Florida residents. In this company: visitor driver license or ID numbers (SYS-11), employee Social Security numbers (SYS-12), and any biometric data (501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VI); none collected today). Whether badge access history counts as 'information regarding an individual's geolocation' (item (VII)) is a question for counsel
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. Clock starts at the determination, not at discovery; record the date
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email; notice must give the date or date range, the data involved, and a contact (501.171(4)(e)). Substitute notice allowed only in the cases in 501.171(4)(f)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, if personal information was accessed. For ransomware limited to the BAS server (operational data and drawings), usually no

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. 15 additional days for individual notice if good cause is given to the department in writing within the 30 days
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with the content listed in 501.171(3)(b)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500+ Florida residents (for example, the visitor ID archive holds tens of thousands of scans)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (as defined in 15 U.S.C. 1681a(p)): timing, distribution, and content of the notices

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination provided to the department within 30 days after the determination; kept for at least 5 years
applies_at_this_tier: Only if counsel supports the determination

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request; the agency may extend or revoke in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains, stores, or processes personal information for the company (visitor management, HR and payroll, access control platform, property management system) has a breach
deadline: The vendor must notify the company no later than 10 days after determining the breach; the company then owes the 501.171(3) and (4) notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Track in vendor contracts; the security addendum asks for 24 hours (POL-01 4.8)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected individuals (tenant employees, visitors, employees) who reside outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residence of every affected individual; the Florida metro area draws few out-of-state residents, but visitors may live anywhere

citation: Lease template (2023 and later) security clause; negotiated 72-hour clauses in 12 leases
trigger: Unauthorized access to tenant employee data held in the access control system
deadline: 12 tenants: within 72 hours as defined in each lease (counsel to confirm when each clause's clock starts; plan from discovery). All other 2023+ leases: promptly. Pre-2023 leases: no clause, but notify with the others
notify: Each tenant's designated contact, by the lease notice method (Property Managers keep the list offline)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal. Also send service interruption notices under each lease if building services are degraded

citation: Merchant agreement; PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.10.1 (SAQ P2PE) incident response plan
trigger: Suspected compromise of card data or tampering with a P2PE terminal
deadline: Per the merchant agreement and the P2PE Instruction Manual (Controller to confirm the time in the agreement)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if card data or terminals are involved. BAS ransomware does not reach the stand-alone P2PE terminals

deadline: Per policy; call the carrier's breach hotline before hiring any vendor so costs are covered

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
citation: CISA CPG 2.0 goal 5.B (voluntary); no statute requires it for this company
trigger: Ransomware or other significant cyber incident
deadline: As soon as practical; the runbook targets within 24 hours of declaration
notify: CISA (incident reporting on cisa.gov) and the FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary. Recommended: it supports OFAC mitigation and may bring technical help

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Statute: 72 hours after reasonable belief of a covered incident; 24 hours after a ransom payment. Not in effect until the final rule is effective
applies_at_this_tier: No. Final rule not published as of 2026-09-26, and the company would not be covered under the NPRM's criteria (P03). Recheck when the final rule is published

trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after the materiality determination
applies_at_this_tier: No. The company is privately held

obligation: Covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment report
citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No. The company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts (confirmed by the COO). Recheck if that changes, because the camera fleet has not been screened for covered brands
